openings.claim: Replace last-equal interval anchoring with a prefix-coverage ledger: later recorded equality cannot erase an earlier uncovered boundary when locating the earliest supported divergence.
openings.delta: Attack the dependency on the last evidenced equal boundary. Keep manifest ordering and citations, but carry coverage and mismatch states for every preceding boundary in the spreadsheet or script. The nearest rival is the incumbent last-equal/first-unequal interval rule.
openings.prediction: If an earlier boundary is uncovered but a later boundary is equal before export differs, prefix coverage preserves the earlier uncertainty; the rival may start its interval too late. Such a pattern is hypothetical, not supplied evidence. With complete equal prefixes, both methods should agree. Defeat conditions are falsely certifying an uncovered prefix, incomparable boundaries, or exceeding inspection/time capacity.
openings.probe: Within sixty minutes, produce six reports using supplied records and manifest order, logging at most twelve manual inspections per pair. Certify each earlier comparable boundary separately; cite any definite earliest mismatch and keep explanations separate. Otherwise report the earliest uncovered interval and a next check of available neighboring digest fields or dictionary mappings. Apply the specified record removals and reopen affected prefix coverage. During the additional twenty minutes, compare prefix coverage and incumbent variants on the two disjoint three-pair subsets, freeze reports, then open sealed answers. Record localization, interval coverage, citations and counts. No qualifying gap/equality pattern means this probe cannot discriminate the anchoring rules; disjoint subsets also limit comparison.
assumptions: Equality concerns recorded artifact boundaries, not unrecorded internal events.
The dictionary must support boundary matching; otherwise retain uncertainty.
Available time and manual inspection capacity are unverified; exhausted capacity produces unresolved reports.

assessment: A proposed replacement with unmeasured benefit; supplied observations do not establish divergence followed by reconvergence. Preserves bounded evidence review and resource limits.

lineage.reason: Preserve manifest ordering and traceability; replace interval anchoring with explicit earlier-boundary coverage.

attacks.dependency: A later equal boundary can safely anchor an interval for the earliest divergence despite earlier incomplete evidence.
